chapter.title_fa: چگونه واقعاً در شطرنج برنده شویم

diagrams.book_context: The chapter recalls the standard initial chess position before explaining how games are won.
diagrams.implementation_notes: This exact image asset is reused on PDF page 55 (Chapter Two). In the app render the board from FEN; do not ship the source bitmap as the board UI.

diagrams.book_context: The simplest checkmate example: Black king e8, White queen e7, White king e6.
diagrams.implementation_notes: Position is shown as a checkmate example. No move sequence is printed for reaching it. Use as a static teaching position unless a separate move sequence is authored and reviewed.

diagrams.book_context: Four-piece checkmate: White bishop g7, White king g6, White knight h6; Black king h8.
diagrams.implementation_notes: Black king square h8 is highlighted in red in the source diagram. The caption explains the White bishop attack and king/knight coverage.

diagrams.book_context: A fully populated-board checkmate example; Black king is on d4 and is attacked by White's pieces.
diagrams.move_history: not provided in this chapter; castling rights are not inferable from a single position
diagrams.implementation_notes: FEN castling rights deliberately set to '-' because the diagram does not provide the prior move history needed to prove whether White retained castling rights. Do not infer castling rights from piece placement alone.

diagrams.book_context: The final Scholar's Mate position after White checkmates Black in four moves.
diagrams.move_history: candidate canonical line; the chapter shows the final position and says mate occurs in four moves, but does not print this full line
diagrams.implementation_notes: The PGN line is an added instructional reconstruction, not quoted from this chapter. Validate the replay in a chess rules engine before release.

diagrams.book_context: Fool's Mate: Black queen on h4 has checkmated the White king in two moves.
diagrams.move_history: candidate canonical line; the chapter says two moves and shows the final position, but does not print the full move list
diagrams.implementation_notes: The PGN line is an added instructional reconstruction, not quoted from this chapter. Validate the replay in a chess rules engine before release.

diagrams.book_context: The resignation position from Game 11 of the 2014 World Chess Championship, Carlsen (White) vs Anand (Black).
diagrams.implementation_notes: The full game PGN is sourced externally because the chapter itself only shows the final position. External source: https://www.schakers.info/?p=5864. The game ended 1-0 after 45.Kc3.

diagrams.book_context: Black has a large material advantage; the text asks the reader to find either of two checkmates if it were Black to move.
diagrams.move_history: two solutions printed in the book's footnote: Qh8# or Qh2#
diagrams.implementation_notes: Exercise prompt and both solutions are source-supported. Accept either move as correct. Add feedback only after the move is made.

diagrams.book_context: Almost the same position as the preceding diagram, except White no longer has the pawn on g5; the text explains a draw if Black flags.
diagrams.implementation_notes: The difference from BD-032 is exactly the missing White pawn on g5. No playable sequence is needed; present as a visual comparison.

diagrams.book_context: The Steinitz–von Bardeleben position from Hastings 1895, after White's rook move to h7+; von Bardeleben left the playing hall.
diagrams.implementation_notes: External FIDE Museum material confirms Black to move for the famous position; an external historical PGN gives the played score through 25.Rxh7+. External sources: https://museum.fide.com/champions/wilhelm-steinitz and https://www.devonjuniorchess.co.uk/content/hastings-1895. Do not append the post-game demonstration variation as if it were played.
